chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the tick is not from the camel, and the tick-bite (or swelling) on the camel is like the lice on your body; therefore, do not cast it off, and cast off the ticks.

key_terms.الْحَلَمَةُ: Tick-bite or the swelling caused by a tick
key_terms.الْقُرَادَ: Ticks (specifically the type to be killed)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing ticks and removing tick bites while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling to clarify the juristic distinction between the insect itself and the resulting wound, using the analogy of lice on the human body to illustrate that the swelling is an integral part of the animal. This distinction is crucial for determining whether the pilgrim incurs expiation (kaffarah) for killing the creature, as the 'tick' is considered a distinct entity while the 'swelling' is merely a bodily feature. The hadith thus refines the application of Ihram prohibitions by separating the pest from its physical effect on the host.
